review_type: Fresh independent source, actual-clause coverage, scope and effective-key challenge
scope: Original Mayfair2010/2013 English2–4-player BASE plus positively applicable previous-Mayfair unified base clarifications. No Up!, Underworld, Americana, Con Jobs, revised2024 six-player rules, or optional Gamble Variant.
conclusion: All38 actual questions have correct in-scope required facts. Complete procedural and branch challenge found no genuinely unasked consequential rule branch. Final ledger passes16 and17 each add zero; stopping rule is satisfied.

per_question_scope_and_key_checks.actual_asked_question: How are starting properties and money assigned, where do the dealt cards go, and how is the End of Game card inserted?
required_facts_checked: Remove End of Game, shuffle, deal two property cards per player.
Mark the two initial lots and take starting money equal to the sum of their printed card money values.
Discard by color/Strip with counts visible.
Divide remaining shuffled deck into four roughly equal stacks; End of Game on top of fourth, other three on top.
per_question_scope_and_key_checks.source_and_scope_check: Setup property assignment, initial money, discarded-card destinations/visibility, and End card placement are all directly asked. The setup-only reuse restriction is correctly background here and asked in Q03.
per_question_scope_and_key_checks.source_evidence: Original p2 Setting Up; unified physical p5.

per_question_scope_and_key_checks.actual_asked_question: Who takes the first turn, how does turn order proceed, and what is the normal Draw/Play sequence?
required_facts_checked: Each rolls two dice; highest roller takes player card and first turn.
Pass player card left after each turn.
Draw property card, take its lot, pay all owned lots, pay/score indicated casinos, discard appropriately, then Play actions.
per_question_scope_and_key_checks.source_and_scope_check: Directly asks opening actor selection (two dice, highest roller), leftward player-card succession, and Draw takeover, lots, casino payout/scoring, discard, Play order. No expansion draw step is imported.
per_question_scope_and_key_checks.source_evidence: Original p2 Taking Turns/On Every Turn; original p3 Ending Step 1; unified physical pp6–9 filtered for base.

per_question_scope_and_key_checks.actual_asked_question: You draw the card for an empty lot. When is it acquired and paid, and do the printed card starting-money values pay again?
required_facts_checked: Place your marker before payouts.
The newly acquired marked lot pays you $1 in the coming lot payout.
Card money values are used only during setup, not drawn-turn income.
per_question_scope_and_key_checks.source_and_scope_check: The empty-lot acquisition branch places a marker before the next lot payout, yielding $1; initial card cash does not recur. Does not require a recital of other lots.
per_question_scope_and_key_checks.source_evidence: Original p2 Setting Up/Take Over Your Lot/Owned Lots Pay.

per_question_scope_and_key_checks.actual_asked_question: You draw a lot card for a sprawled tile with an opponent’s 5, although the board prints 2. What happens to the tile and die, and who receives its imminent matching-color money?
required_facts_checked: Tile stays; replace opposing die with your own retaining current value 5, not printed 2.
Acquisition precedes payouts, so you receive $5 for that die when its casino pays.
per_question_scope_and_key_checks.source_and_scope_check: Opponent-owned sprawled tile retains the tile and current pip value 5; replacement occurs before its payout, so the new owner receives $5. Printed value2 is not reapplied.
per_question_scope_and_key_checks.source_evidence: Original p2 Take Over Your Lot/Money Paid; unified physical p7.

per_question_scope_and_key_checks.actual_asked_question: When do same-color tiles form one casino, can they be divided, and is the boss determined by total pips or something else?
required_facts_checked: Edge-connected same-color tiles on same block form a single indivisible casino; diagonal-only contact does not.
Boss is owner of highest individual die, not greatest total pips or most tiles.
per_question_scope_and_key_checks.source_and_scope_check: Directly asks casino connectivity and indivisibility, plus individual highest die versus total influence. Same-block and edge criteria, and diagonal exclusion, are source-defined. Player/casino color independence remains background.
per_question_scope_and_key_checks.source_evidence: Original p1 Casino Tiles/Player Dice; original p2 Who Owns What.

per_question_scope_and_key_checks.actual_asked_question: A three-tile gold casino contains Red 5 and Blue 3 and 2; Red also owns two marked lots. On a gold payout, how much money and how many points does each receive from these holdings?
required_facts_checked: Red receives $7: $5 die plus $2 lots.
Blue receives $5 from dice.
Red boss receives 3 casino points, Blue no casino points.
per_question_scope_and_key_checks.source_and_scope_check: Directly asked calculation: Red $5 from die plus $2 from lots equals $7; Blue $3+$2=$5; Red highest5 earns nominal3 casino points, Blue0. No track position is supplied, so3 is the award rather than an invented final score.
per_question_scope_and_key_checks.source_evidence: Original p2 Owned Lots Pay/Money Paid/Points Earned.

per_question_scope_and_key_checks.actual_asked_question: How does Pay The Strip differ from a color payout, and what qualifies a casino whose only one tile touches The Strip?
required_facts_checked: Color pays all casinos of that color anywhere.
Strip pays all colors with at least one casino edge adjacent to Strip.
Entire qualifying casino pays money/points for all tiles, not only touching tile.
per_question_scope_and_key_checks.source_and_scope_check: Directly contrasts color-anywhere payout with any-color Strip-edge eligibility, and explicitly tests whole-casino payout when only one constituent tile touches.
per_question_scope_and_key_checks.source_evidence: Original p2 Pay Based on Color/Pay The Strip/Money Paid/Points Earned; unified physical p8.

per_question_scope_and_key_checks.actual_asked_question: Which actions may you take in Play, in what order and how often, and may another player perform an action on your turn?
required_facts_checked: Build, sprawl, remodel, reorganize, gamble in any order.
All may repeat except gamble once per own turn; reorganization also limited per die per turn.
No player takes actions on another player’s turn.
per_question_scope_and_key_checks.source_and_scope_check: Names the five base actions, free choice of order/repetition, gamble once and per-die reorganization limit. The off-turn action prohibition is explicitly asked. No raise/acquire action or trading-as-action is added.

per_question_scope_and_key_checks.actual_asked_question: How do you build on your marked lot whose board price is $6 and printed die is 2? State cost, marker and die handling, and tile choice.

per_question_scope_and_key_checks.actual_asked_question: You boss a gold casino and want to sprawl onto an edge-adjacent empty unowned $9 lot with printed die 3. What do you pay and place, and may you instead sprawl onto an opponent’s marked lot or a merely diagonal lot?
required_facts_checked: Pay $18, place available gold tile with own die 3.
The stated eligible lot is empty/unowned and edge-adjacent; opponent-marked and diagonal-only targets are illegal.
Cannot sprawl without available tile of same color.

per_question_scope_and_key_checks.actual_asked_question: How does remodeling a two-tile casino work, including eligibility, cost, tile supply, and a merger with a neighboring casino whose highest die beats yours?
required_facts_checked: Must boss casino; remodel all its tiles into one new color with enough available tiles.
Pay $10 ($5 each); replace all tiles with new-color tiles; dice/holdings remain.
Edge-adjacent same-color casinos merge; owner of larger die becomes boss even if another player.
Return replaced old-color tiles to their supply.
per_question_scope_and_key_checks.source_and_scope_check: Eligibility is explicitly asked: actor must boss the casino, change all tiles to one new sufficiently supplied color, $10 for two tiles. Holdings persist; old tiles return to supply; edge merger makes the given stronger neighbor boss.

per_question_scope_and_key_checks.actual_asked_question: May a non-boss with one die reorganize a casino with dice 5, 3 and 2? State who pays how much, which dice roll and who rolls them, and where multiple dice may return.
required_facts_checked: Yes, at least one own die suffices; acting player pays $10 total pips of all dice.
All dice reroll, each owner rolling their own.
Each owner returns dice only to their own original tiles, choosing assignment among those tiles if multiple.
per_question_scope_and_key_checks.source_and_scope_check: Directly tests non-boss eligibility with own die, actor paying all10 pips, all owners rerolling all their dice, and assignment only among each owner’s original tiles. Multiple-die return is expressly asked despite one die for acting player.
per_question_scope_and_key_checks.source_evidence: Original p3 Reorganize; unified physical p11.

per_question_scope_and_key_checks.actual_asked_question: A die was reorganized earlier this turn and its casino then merges into a larger casino. Can the larger casino be reorganized this turn, and are free boss-tie rerolls prohibited too?
required_facts_checked: No: no die may be reorganized more than once per turn, so any previously reorganized die prevents reorganization of the enlarged casino.
Boss-tie rerolls are free and not subject to reorganization once-per-turn limit.
per_question_scope_and_key_checks.source_and_scope_check: Tests the consequential merger restriction: any already reorganized die blocks a new reorganization of its enlarged casino this turn. Unlimited necessary free boss rerolls are a separate mechanism.

per_question_scope_and_key_checks.actual_asked_question: After a merger, Red 5 and Blue 5 tie above Green 4. What rerolls, at what cost, and who bosses if both 5s reroll to 3? What if all largest tied dice belong to one player, or only smaller dice tie?
required_facts_checked: Immediately reroll only tied largest dice at no cost.
If both become 3, Green unchanged 4 is boss; do not keep rerolling smaller 3s.
Same-player highest tie requires no reroll; ties below highest require none.
If different players remain tied for current highest, repeat with current highest until one player controls highest.
per_question_scope_and_key_checks.source_and_scope_check: Tests immediate free current-highest cross-player rerolls, repeat on remaining current-highest ties, Green4 becoming boss after both5s become3, same-owner tied maxima exemption, and no lower-tie rerolls. Termination at one controlling player is supported by unified clarification and original same-owner exception.

per_question_scope_and_key_checks.actual_asked_question: You have $18 and gamble at an opponent’s four-tile casino whose boss has $15. What is the maximum bet, who gets the House card, and how many times may you gamble this turn?
required_facts_checked: Maximum $15: minimum of $20 tile cap, own $18 and boss $15.
Gamble once during own turn.
Give the casino boss the House card.
per_question_scope_and_key_checks.source_and_scope_check: The requested maximum is min($20 tile cap,$18 gambler,$15 boss)=$15; House card to boss; gamble once this turn. Opponent-boss eligibility is given here and separately tested in Q30.

required_facts_checked: 3/4/9/10/11: win $4 from boss and retain/get stake back.
2/12: nominal win $8 but receive only boss’s available $7 and retain/get stake back.
5/6/7/8: lose/pay $4 to boss.

per_question_scope_and_key_checks.actual_asked_question: What may be traded, when may trading occur, how are traded lots and dice transferred, and what cannot be promised or traded?
required_facts_checked: Trade money, lots, casino dice and actions on the active player’s current turn. Trading may occur even off-turn, except no initiated trades during unresolved boss ties or after End of Game is drawn.
Replace lot marker with recipient marker; replace die with recipient die at same current pip value, not board value.
No points or casino tiles; no promises of future-turn actions/exchanges/transfers.
No actions on another player’s turn.
per_question_scope_and_key_checks.source_and_scope_check: Broad actual what/when/how/prohibited questions support base assets, current-turn actions only, off-turn trading, both explicit timing exceptions, replacement marker/die at existing pips, no points/tiles, no future-turn promises, and no off-turn action.
per_question_scope_and_key_checks.source_evidence: Original p4 Trading; unified physical pp9,15,16.

per_question_scope_and_key_checks.actual_asked_question: Starting at score 8, where do single casino awards of 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 points leave you? Can two separate one-tile casinos combine their awards, and in what order are different casinos scored?
required_facts_checked: 1 leaves 8; 2 or 3 reaches 10; 4 or 5 reaches 12.
Insufficient excess at a break is lost; cannot pool separate casino awards.
Score each casino independently smallest to largest, player chooses equal-size order; two single-tile awards leave 8.

per_question_scope_and_key_checks.actual_asked_question: What happens when the End of Game card is drawn, including remaining actions, final payouts, winner and tied score? Is there an immediate alternative win condition?

Final payout all owned lots and casinos touching Strip, with ordinary money and scoring rules.
Most points wins; tied most points breaks by most money.
90+ points wins immediately in base game.

per_question_scope_and_key_checks.actual_asked_question: In two-player play, what happens to F cards drawn during setup and during a turn? May anyone build on F, and can a turn pay more than once before actions?
required_facts_checked: No building on F block.
Setup F card is discarded and replaced; valid two cards determine initial properties/money.
During turn do not mark F; pay owned lots and indicated casinos/points, discard then repeat Draw until A–E card resolved.
Each such draw pays, so multiple payouts occur in one turn before Play.
per_question_scope_and_key_checks.source_and_scope_check: Explicitly asks both setup and in-turn F branches: discard/replace during setup, no F marker or building, pay/score/discard and redraw during turn until A–E; multiple payouts before Play. per_question_scope_and_key_checks.source_evidence: Original p4 Two-player/Winning; unified physical p16 Two-player.

per_question_scope_and_key_checks.actual_asked_question: All nine gold tiles are on the board. Can you build another gold tile using the spare tenth tile, sprawl a gold casino, or remodel a three-tile casino to gold? May you build a different available color?

per_question_scope_and_key_checks.actual_asked_question: Next to a casino you boss is an edge-adjacent, built casino tile of another color with no die. Is it a legal Sprawl target because it is unowned, or must the target be an empty lot?
required_facts_checked: No. A built casino tile remains on the board even without a die; it is a casino space, not an empty lot. Sprawl requires an empty, unowned lot, so you cannot sprawl onto or replace this tile.
